utterances.text: No, I've never met him, and his name meant nothing to me after we had learned what had happened down there. Until then, I didn't know of him; I didn't know his name. I only knew that they were in touch with some persons in order to locate and find the people that they were interested in recruiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when these reservists were engaged in March 1999, did you know that in the areas of the former Yugoslavia -- actually, did you know whether they had committed any crimes in any other parts of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior and I had no information of any of those reservists, if they had stayed in any conflict areas outside the borders of Serbia, had committed any type of crime. Had we had such information, they would not have been included into the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After the events in Podujevo, when was it that you heard for the first time that certain members of the reserve force committed certain crimes in the territory of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about that for the first time during the Milosevic trial here, when a footage was shown. I followed that trial, and that was the first time that I was informed about the crime they committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time of their engagement in the reserve force in March 1999, what information did you have about where those people had come from and what kind of persons they were?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I personally had no information whatsoever about how many of them had any previous combat experience and where they hailed from. I didn't know any of them, and I did not participate in their selection. For me it was important that the unit be provided with a reserve force so that it could perform its duties. As for its personnel, that was something that was outside my field of interest. That was done by other services at lower levels. I was not included in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't mean you personally, but having discussions with different people, some of which you referred to, did you know where those people were from and what their experience was which would qualify them to become reservists of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of that from Trajkovic. He told me that he knew some of them from the times when he was in the area of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Sirmium. He did, however, say there were only a few of them that he knew and that most of them had no previous experience having hailed from Sid, Novi Sad, and some other towns in the area. He didn't tell me what the number of those who had previous experience is and how many of them had none. He just told me that he knew some of them. In any case, that was the extent of the information I had, and it came exclusively from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Given that this reserve force was supposed to be attached to the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit, how did it come about that people were engaged for whom it was unknown whether they had any previous experience that would be necessary to become a part of the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Yugoslavia was under attack, the FRY that is. We had to make use of any people we had available in order for the unit to be able to complete its tasks. They did not need any special training or knowledge of weapons with a view to performing the tasks Trajkovic had envisaged for them. They were supposed to be there simply to secure any Special Anti-Terrorist Unit facilities or to man the front lines previously reached by the professional staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next please have D010-0692.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is a 65 ter document 158 and tab 136 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There seems to be a mistake. 65 ter 1581 and D009 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Djordjevic [sic] please repeat the last four digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat. D -- yes, this is the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we see here a report on the engagement of the reserve force of the SAJ signed by Commander Mr. Trajkovic. In the heading of the document -- can you read it out to us.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the document you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please read the one that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the document. It's the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D009-0785. That's the right number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, while we're looking for the document - and we'll go back to it later - could you please tell us what were the circumstances under which this report saw the light of day, and do you know why it was put together and who was supposed to receive it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of the interior wanted to receive a more detailed report on the engagement of the reserve force for the needs of the SAJ, hence he ordered me to ask the commander of the unit to draft a detailed report about everything that had to do with engagement of the reserve force for the need of the SAJ. When the SAJ unit and the commander returned from Kosovo, I ordered him accordingly. He drafted a report that he sent to me, and I, in turn, forwarded it to the minister. It contains all the elements that have to do with the engagement of the reserve force for the needs of the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D010-8692.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that's happening, could the report be Exhibit P86?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that P86 is only a version of the document that the OTP has. I found that entire document with a heading, stating the Ministry of the Interior, and indicating who drafted it. I wanted to put that to the witness to comment. On the first page, there is a part that was not translated in the version that was admitted into evidence. This is a more complete version of the text. This would be a full document. That is why I asked for the D document. This document was disclosed to us by the OTP when they were disclosing these documents for the second time. I also came across such documents in Belgrade, and, in particular, this complete document with the stamp. That is why I am asking for D010-8692 to be put on the screen. Ms. O'Leary, do we have this document in e-court? Ms. O'Leary confirms, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What number is it on the 65 ter list, if you could kindly give us that information, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 0581 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1581.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- on the Defence list. This is it in B/C/S. We have it in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the heading, Mr. Djordjevic, can you tell us which organisational unit drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was put together by the special anti-terrorist group on the 13th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to the second page of the document. It seems like in the English version I still need a portion that is on the first side -- page. Can you scroll down in the B/C/S, please. The English is fine now, and I see the top of the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the first four lines of the second page in Serbian. In English it is the fifth paragraph, the first four lines.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 27th of March, 1999, at about 1600 [as interpreted] hours, on the approval of the MUP staff and with the chief of the service being advised, Zoran Simovic, SAJ commander Belgrade, went to Prolom Banja in order to take over members of the reserve force to be engaged."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are two parts of the document which were not translated as part of the exhibit that was admitted into evidence. It was illegible, and, as such, these portions were not translated. Therefore, I propose that this complete document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Line 52, line 22, the English transcript suggests that it was 1600 hours. The original appears to be 1800 hours. That having been noted, this will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D442.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we hear of the Skorpions here all the time as a unit that was attached to the SAJ as a reserve force. In 1999, had you heard of that name, the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time of the engagement when Trajkovic informed me of this, the name of Skorpions was not mentioned anywhere. Later on, this was linked with Slobodan Medic, who indeed had had a unit which, in the territory of Slavonia, performed certain tasks and that was their name. However, in their communication with me, it was never mentioned. I didn't know of that name. All I was interested in was that special unit had ensured a certain number of reservists that could be engaged for certain purposes. So this name, the name of the unit following us, learning of all the misdeeds that they had committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, this name emerged only after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see the lists of the reserve forces in their records, and did anyone inform you of that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody informed us either of the names or of any information as to who was placed in the reserve forces. As I have told you, I was told by the police administration and later on by Trajkovic that a certain number of persons was located, that they were put on their reserve forces, and that later that they were engaged to carry out certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, when the war began, was there any relocation within the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We, within the ministry, knew that all facilities of the ministry, both in Belgrade and throughout the territory of Serbia, would be a target for attacks of NATO forces. This is why an order was issued, both in the secretariats and within the seat of the ministry, to abandon the premises that had been used until that time for our work. And we were practically spread out through a number of facilities, a number of locations - I'm now talking about the seat of the ministry - so a number of locations throughout Belgrade, and the same applied to all the secretariats. They abandoned their facilities and went to other facilities based on old plans, and they conducted their work in these other facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us something about the communication between the seat of the MUP and various SUPs in the territory of Serbia, outside of Kosovo and Metohija during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communication was -- went mostly via telephone, which was operational until the relay centres were destroyed, the relay centres used by the ministry for radio communication, and depending on which telephone centre in which secretariat was hit. That is to say that technical services for communications within the ministry did their best so that in those circumstances where relay towers and so on were destroyed, they could provide communication with the ministry either via direct telephone communication or via patching and making other channels, creating other channels, which I really don't know much about in the technical sense. I can tell you that our communication with the secretariats in the territory of Serbia outside of Kosovo was extremely difficult in those times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there a courier service?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The courier service existed back in normal times, that is to say that twice a week a courier would bring mail from all secretariats and then take the mail from the seat of the ministry, the mail that was theirs. And this was continued during the war so that certain documents reached the seat of the ministry and various SUPs via courier service. When the regular communication channels were disrupted, couriers were used more frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any collegium meetings held during the war, collegium being senior staff members; and if so, what was discussed at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as in regular times, even in those special times, collegium meetings were held at which chiefs of various administrations informed the minister about the situation, the security situation, in their jurisdictions, mostly focusing on the consequences of bombing campaign as well as the participation of ministry units in providing assistance and in any action taken during the bombing - I'm now referring to the entire territory of Serbia - and the ministry, in addition to these extraordinary tasks, had to conduct its regular routine tasks: ensuring law and order, providing security at the state border, issuing passports, IDs, driver's licences, and so on. So even under those difficult conditions, they had to conduct their regular public security tasks, and they needed to inform the minister of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at these collegium meetings, was there any discussion of planning and conducting various anti-terrorist operations in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never any discussion at collegium meetings of specific concrete tasks of the special unit or unit for special operations down there in Kosovo, nor were reports on that matter provided at collegium meetings. The only issues that were reported on were logistical issues that the administration for joint affairs of police had to carry out. So they would perhaps inform about the equipment, communication channels, and they would also inform on whether there were any casualties among the ranks of policemen down there in Kosovo. So that was the only topic that they provided information on at the collegium meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there any special meetings where planning and conducting of anti-terrorist operations was discussed, and did you attend any such meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such meetings were never organised at the seat of the ministry, nor was there anyone who could have briefed on that because that information was available only to the staff down there. And the staff was the only body that could have informed of it. It never happened that any anti-terrorist or combat plans or their implementation was discussed at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: During the war, were you informed about the staff in Pristina, about planning or conducting any anti-terrorist operations?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have gone over all types of information provided from the staff to the ministry, and everything that I was informed of was contained in the reports that we received in that way. I was practically informed of all instances where police members were killed, because I sent condolences cables on behalf of the ministry. However, throughout the war, I never received any sort of a plan nor did I take part in planning any anti-terrorist or combat activity against any kind of forces in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you ever receive any report in any form from them about the actions planned and conducted, carried out, by them?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not informed either of planned activities or any action they took pursuant to those plans, that is to say that nobody was duty-bound to inform me of this nor was I informed of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's time for our technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume in an hour's time at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.34 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, could you please tell us, when did you and how did you learn of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the question. The interpreters didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 6th of April --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please stop. My question was: When and from whom did you learn for the first time of the existence of bodies? And please tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first information on the existence of bodies reached me on the 6th of April after 2000 hours from Caslav Golubovic, chief of the secretariat. He called me at that time and said that on the bank of the Danube in an area near Tekija there was a refrigeration truck with 20-odd bodies, that municipal prosecutor was informed of it, and that several prosecutors and an investigating judge went to the site, as well as some of the operatives from the office in Kladovo, under whose jurisdiction this area comes. At that time, he also informed me that when the municipal prosecutors realised that there were a number of bodies there, they left the site, saying that they would inform the district prosecutor. Caslav told me that the police had also informed the district prosecutor's office too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me what SUP did Caslav head?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secretariat of the Interior in Bor. He was the chief of that secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please tell us what happened then and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that as for any further action, he needed to wait because at that time for me that was a significant event and that upon learning of it, I was duty-bound to inform minister about it so that we could see what to do with the bodies that had been found. This is to say that I was really taken aback by this information, and I, following that, went to the minister; and I informed him of everything that I had learned from the chief of the secretariat, namely, that bodies had been found in a refrigerator truck, bodies which, based on their clothing, resembled bodies from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. He also told me that on the truck there was a sign, the name of a company which was from the territory of Kosovo. So immediately upon learning of it, I informed the minister about it. And after a detailed briefing where I conveyed everything I knew, I asked for instructions on what to do further. He ordered me to convey to the chief of the secretariat that following the routine procedure, the bodies were to be buried in an area where they had been found. He also instructed me to tell the chief of the secretariat that all further action in relation to this should be kept confidential so that the public was not informed. He told me this without commenting on any of the information which I had conveyed to him about the event. So without any comments he --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me interrupt you. Would you please tell me, at that point in time, where was the ministry located, or rather, the facilities, the premises, where you worked?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After moving out from the seat of the ministry, we changed seven to eight locations at least. I think that at this point we were located at the bank premises in Lole Ribara Street. I know that after every relocation my office was always next to the minister's office whenever we changed locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me about other administrations, where were they?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever we found appropriate premises. So administrations were spread out throughout the town in various locations. Joint affairs administration with assistant Zekovic and the entire financial service were in one location as well as the assistant minister in charge of that area. Crime investigations police had their own location, and in our location, in addition to the minister, we also had Misic assistant minister's office. So we were spread out in different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now tell me what happened after this conversation you had with the minister.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called Caslav Golubovic, and I conveyed to him the instructions of the minister, that following the procedure, the routine procedure, the bodies were to be buried in the immediate vicinity of the location where they had been found. I also conveyed the instruction concerning the media. This means that in my conversation with him I made it clear to him that this was an instruction from the minister that I conveyed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After your conversation with Mr. Golubovic, what did you do next in the ministry in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that with the emergence of these bodies was of a surprise for me, and I wanted to clarify this matter with the minister in some way. I wanted to establish with him what this was exactly all about. According to the initial reports, it seems that according to the vehicle where the bodies were found and according to the clothes, that those were persons from Kosovo and Metohija. And judging by the clothes, they were specifically ethnic Albanians. So having all that in mind, I wanted this situation to be clarified. And I reiterated that in my conversation with the minister. And I suggested that we should establish a commission or a group who would investigate the whole matter and to see how it happened for those bodies to be found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us when you had this conversation that you just retailed to us?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took place immediately after I conveyed these instructions to the chief of the SUP on how to proceed. These instructions had to be issued to him because all these people were there gathered on the bank of the river Danube, therefore he should be made aware of how to act. After I conveyed these instructions from the minister to him, I wanted to clarify with the minister exactly what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what else did you discuss with the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that the situation as it was required a full check and that all the facts needed to be established. I suggested that he set up this commission or a group to investigate that. He didn't respond to my suggestion at all. Then I proposed that I myself would set up such a group to investigate the situation. Only after he had realised that I was committed to taking steps in order to clarify the whole matter, he made it known to me that he was fully behind it; that certain incidents had happened down there; and that something should be done in order to prevent the revelation of the finding of these bodies because of the whole NATO campaign and bombing. And he also added that no further measures should be undertaken in order to establish the true facts, that is to say to establish the origin of the bodies and how they were killed. So at that point in time, his decisions were such. But, nevertheless, he instructed me to act with the chief of the secretariat and to keep him apprised of everything that I hear from the chief and about everything that was of importance and to inform him about everything without any delay. Based on this conclusion of his and his explanation, I left his office and proceeded with doing some other jobs because there was another bombing strike during that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you speak later on the phone with Mr. Golubovic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think we spoke on the phone twice after that. And in this first conversation, Golubovic said that during this operation of pulling out the refrigerator truck from the water, because it was partially drowned in water, they noticed that in addition to these 20-odd bodies that there were additional bodies. He suspected, or rather, he told me that in the area of his secretariat and with the resources that they had, it was not possible to carry out the proper procedure, that is to say the autopsy of the bodies and later their burial, given the number of the bodies that had emerged from this refrigerator truck. So he proposed for this procedure to be carried out either in Belgrade or in Nis where they had better conditions for all this to be completed. However, I insisted, pursuant to the former order of the minister, be -- that this be conducted since the situation changed and since the minister instructed me to keep him updated all the time. After that, I went to see the minister again, told him that the situation had changed in the intervening period, and that practically the whole procedure as I had been told would be able to be carried out in the area where the bodies were discovered and that the chief of the secretariat was adamant that these bodies should be transported either to Belgrade or Nis for the procedure to be conducted as is the normal case in such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your conversations with the minister, did he give you any more details about where the bodies had come from, and did he impart any new information to you?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There was no additional information apart from the information I received in the first conversation when I insisted on establishing the facts and when he said to me what he said, that he was behind it. He didn't offer any further details relating to the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself insist on his providing additional information and did he comply?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had these conversations every time we were in contact because I wanted any sort of information because I knew that I had nothing to do with this business, neither did I know how these people died nor where they were buried, where and how they were dug up, how they were transported, et cetera. I knew nothing about it. So due to that, I insisted that he gave me more details. But after what he had told me, he didn't offer any information that I wanted to hear. So that is how I reacted and this is how we had these conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After this conversation with Mr. Golubovic in which it was stated that those bodies could not be buried there and the whole procedure was not to be conducted in Kladovo, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I conveyed the opinion of the secretariat's chief and the proposals that he had made, and then the minister instructed me to point out to him that he should find a vehicle, load the bodies into it, and to send it to Belgrade. After that, I told Caslav what he had been ordered to do and added that the minister said that Caslav should only provide telephone numbers of the drivers who are going to drive the vehicles for transportation in order for them to get in touch with him and what the final destination was going to be. The minister also told me that the location where the bodies were going to be transferred would be his concern, and the only thing he told me was to tell Caslav that those bodies should be loaded into a truck and that the refrigerator truck from which they had been extracted should be destroyed. That's what I did. I passed on this instruction to Golubovic, but he told me that he only had one truck and that it was not enough for all the bodies, that he needed another vehicle but that he couldn't provide it. I told him that, according to the previous order, he should send the vehicle with as many bodies as they were able to put into it, and as for another vehicle, I was going to see what can be done because, as I said, there were bodies still lying there on the ground. The whole situation was - how shall I put it? - very frustrating for me as well and very unpleasant, and my patience was running out. After that, I went to see the minister again. And, on that occasion, I told him that until then I definitely had nothing to do with the whole affair and afterwards I wouldn't want to interfere and have anything to do with it anymore. I gave him Golubovic's number, and I said that somebody should contact him and see where the bodies were going to be transported. I also told him that another truck needed to be sent down there to collect the remaining bodies. And, practically, I said that as far as I was concerned, I didn't want to have anything to do with that anymore; and in light of all my duties and responsibilities that I had vis-à-vis some other territory, not Kosovo, that I didn't want to be part of that any longer. With this, all my contacts with the minister and with Caslav Golubovic were over at that point as far as I was concerned. After that, I never spoke to Caslav again nor did I insist with the minister on clarifying the matters. He only warned me to be careful about what I was doing, that this was a serious matter, and he repeated this story that he told me during our first or second meeting when he said that these were isolated incidents and that at that point this was how it should be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was sufficient for me. I said, All right. Do as you like. I don't wish to take part in this whole matter any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that date, did you receive any information about new bodies? And if you did, can you tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes. A day or two later - I'm not quite sure - the chief from Uzice called me, Djordje Keric, the chief of the Secretariat of the Interior there, and told me that there were a few bodies floating in the Perucac lake on the Drina River. Since there was no other explanation about this, these were generally only official information he had, he said that the regional OUP had been informed. I told him to investigate it and to call me later. When he called me later, he said that in addition to those bodies -- the team that he had sent out onto the ground had told him that in addition to those bodies floating on water, there was a kind of freight box as kind of part of some truck also in the water, and that in that box there were some bodies too. I received this information, and apart from what I had told him earlier to try and investigate more, I didn't instruct him anything specifically because after having received this information, it was my duty to inform the minister. Consequently, I went to see the minister; I conveyed this information to him; I told him who I received it from and what had been found in the water. I told him what my opinion about all that was. He didn't comment; he didn't give me any instructions; and didn't ask me to pass them to anyone. I believed that he was going to settle this matter with someone else, that he wanted to exclude me from the whole matter. And with this conviction, I left his office. After that, the chief of the secretariat Keric called me and told me that all the bodies that had been found in the water and in the vehicle in that area had been buried. I passed this information to the minister without making any comments whatsoever, and I also didn't receive any feedback comment from him. This is as far as this incident on the lake was concerned and the exchange of information I had with the chief from Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many conversations did you have with Keric?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only two. The first one when he informed me about it, when I told him to check what it was about; and the second one when he conveyed to me what else was found in the lake. That was the extent of my communication with that chief of SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did Mr. Keric tell you that the corpses were buried?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the first conversation, a day or two later I think -- in any case, the very next conversation we had was when he told me that the bodies were taken out of the water and buried next to the dam.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether that was it in terms of the information you have about the existence of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shortly after the event at Perucac, I received a phone call from the minister, perhaps a day or two later, telling me that the trucks that were used to transport the bodies from the Danube and Tekija were in the area where the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit had its training compound. He told me that the trucks were there and that the bodies from the Danube were still there. There was again a discussion, and he told me that he was fully aware of me telling him that I no longer wanted to be involved in that situation and that I, on two occasions, refused to carry out his orders, but that this was a very serious situation. He wasn't specific about anything in terms of where the bodies had come from, but he simply told me that the bodies needed to be buried in the area of the training compound where the trucks were. He reminded me that there was a war going on, that Serbia was being attacked, and that there was a lot of destruction, and that this was the way to resolve the situation with the bodies in Batajnica. Having in mind the entire situation in which Serbia was at the time, that is to say there were air-strikes, destruction throughout the territory, as well as having in mind the instructions I had received, I gave in and followed his instructions and orders. I asked him what was I to do from that point on. He said that since I was already familiar with the matter and that I knew from our previous contacts that these were bodies which came from Kosovo and Metohija, in other words, that these were the bodies of Albanians, that it was necessary to bury them and that I should convey to those from the special unit that they should bury them in their training compound. He also told me that I should tell them that these were victims of NATO air-strikes or dead terrorists and that it was necessary to bury them. He also told me to tell them that an exhumation process would be undertaken later on in order to follow the procedure. At that point in time, he basically issued this order to me to convey that information to those I was supposed to convey orders to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got a phone number of the person who was in charge of the compound. I summoned him to my office. I think I managed to locate him in the evening when I received my orders. And the next morning, he was in my office. I told him about his tasks as it was described to me. I told him that these were the bodies of persons who were killed by air-strikes or in combat with the terrorists and that they should be buried inside the special unit's compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you here for a moment. The person you summoned to your office, where was he located?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the other people in the ministry knew, we were advised that the compound was damaged during an air-strike. We were told that the part of the unit that was supposed to secure the facility was relocated. I didn't know where he was at that point in time, but I did manage to get in touch by phone, asking him to come to my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what followed?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I transmitted that order to him. And as he was leaving my office, we met the minister who was passing down the hall. I told the minister that this was the man who was supposed to wrap up the whole matter, after which he left. Once the bodies were buried, he called me and told me that the thing was finished, that is, that the bodies had been buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into closed session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what ensued?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, things were quiet for a while concerning that topic. After a few days or maybe ten days or so, the minister called me again, twice, as far as I recall, telling me that at the same location there was some other vehicles and that it should be resolved the same way, i.e., that I should call that commander again and issue him the same orders as before. So everything was clear; there were no special questions in relation to the first instance when I received similar orders. I passed that information on. It was wrapped up, much like in the first case. The commander followed the orders. And after that, I told the minister that he should no longer count on me in such matters and that I was no longer interested in any of it. I told him that bygones were bygones, but that he should not try to involve me in it again because I had done much in the past although I disagreed with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether you had any part in the transport of those bodies from Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of the existence of those bodies in the territory of Serbia for the first time from the Bor SUP chief, Mr. Caslav Golubovic; the second time from Mr. Keric; and on the following two occasions, the minister told me that the bodies were already in the special unit's compound. That is all the information I had about the corpses. I learned about the corpses in each of these instances, either from the chiefs of the secretariats or after they had been transported to the special unit's compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever learn who organised the transport of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I never learned of who was involved in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever learn or were you told by the minister what were the locations that those bodies came from and how they were killed?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never discussed any particular locations. He never told me they come from this or that area; I simply didn't know that. The only explanation I was given was the one that I have shared with you, and that was that it involved certain incidents. That was the extent of his explanation, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that the minister told you on two more occasions that there were bodies in the Batajnica compound. Did you ever discuss that matter later with him?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during the war. After the war, on one occasion, after having discussed the issue with Trajkovic, I spoke with him. I asked him, What will happen with the problem? And he told me not to worry, that it was his concern, and that he would do as he deemed fit. That was the end of my inquiry into the matter vis-à-vis him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, having heard all you said, can you tell us what your opinion or position was on the matter?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was greatly dissatisfied with such a turn of events, especially because I was convinced that there was nothing I could have done to prevent such loss of life for the persons involved. I could in no way influence the situation in which they were killed. That is why I felt sorry to have been forced to follow instructions that I did. I have to say that after the arrival of the minister towards the end of his mandate, not only during the war, I was not on good terms with him. And all that may have contributed to perhaps me not paying sufficient attention. I was greatly dissatisfied then, and, of course, it will stay with me for the rest of my days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, the war started on the 24th of March, 1999. Can you tell us, did you visit Kosovo; and if you did, when was that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning of the war, or rather, in mid-April, I was twice there, once for a half day and the next time for a full day. So that was in mid-April, and then after that I went down there towards the end of the war, that is to say, after the signing of the Kumanovo Agreement. My visit related to the obligations that were conveyed to the chiefs of secretariat regarding the withdrawal of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when was the first time you went to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was, I think, on the 16th of April. It was a blitz visit by the minister because he wanted to put up an appearance there and to boost the morale and encourage the warriors and the police in Kosovo, as well as the Serbs who were living there. So we had this quick meeting with the chiefs of the secretariat and members of the staff. Also present at this meeting were a couple of politicians. The point of the whole discussion was not the problems existing at the time, but, rather, a press conference in which the minister addressed the media and conveyed to the people, to the population, and to members of the MUP as well to take good care of the people and to encourage them in a way. In that meeting, since there were some personnel problems relating the replacement of two or three chiefs of secretariats, I took the opportunity to hand in two decisions to the chiefs of secretariat who were present there. After that meeting and the press conference, we returned to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that these decisions were handed in to someone. Can you tell us more about it, what kind of decisions you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the decisions on appointment of chiefs of Pristina, Urosevac, and Kosovska Mitrovica secretariats that had been issued by the minister as well as the decisions on the termination of office of chiefs of Mitrovica and Pristina secretariats that I signed by minister's authority, and I took this opportunity to hand over this decision to Mr. Petric, the chief of Pristina secretariat; Cvetic of Kosovska Mitrovica; and I also handed over the decision to Bogoljub Janicijevic, chief or the future chief of SUP Pristina who had been chief of the Urosevac SUP. In absence of other chiefs who were appointed, such as Mr. Janicijevic and Bozidar Filic, these decisions were only later delivered to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood you correctly, you returned to Belgrade on the same day. How did you travel to and from Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the counsel please switch off the microphone while the witness is talking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How and when these decisions were taken? Before that, can you please answer me how you travelled to and from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We rode in cars because it was impossible to use any other means of transportation; airplanes were out of the question because there was war. And as for the decisions on appointment, in these three cases referring to the SUP chiefs were issued by the minister, and the decision on dismissal was issued by me by authority of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we heard about that. But was there any meeting held in Belgrade prior to that and how it was decided to do that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that I understand your question. What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you said who and how passed these decisions, but was that preceded by a meeting in the ministry; and if so, who decided to appoint a number of chiefs and to dismiss others?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decisions on appointment were made by a minister, and these people had already been in their respective posts as chiefs of SUP. And their performance had been taken into account when the minister took this decision, but I cannot recall any specific meeting preceding these decisions. He just made these decisions and issued them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that after this meeting you went back to Pristina a couple of days later. Can you tell us how and why?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was two days later. The minister wanted to see how this hand-over of duties was going on, and he wanted me to oversee this personally in the secretariat in question. I set off in the morning from Belgrade. I first went to the staff HQ, where I report to the head of the staff and other members; after that I went to the Pristina SUP, where I met the chief of the SUP whose office -- term of office had already expired, but he was still there nevertheless. His name was Petric; we had a conversation; and he informed me about a visit that Janicijevic, Bogoljub paid him a visit and that was the man who was supposed to replace him. They discussed the replacement, but they agreed first for the replacement in Urosevac to take place, where Janicijevic was to hand-over his duty and after that the hand-over of duties would be carried out in Pristina. Then I went to Urosevac, where I saw that the hand-over procedure of -- between the former and the future chiefs of secretariats was in progress. I spent some time with them. I monitored how that hand-over was going on. And I learned about the whole procedure. And after that, in the afternoon, I went back to the staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you interested in the hand-over of duty in Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was supposed to go to Kosovska Mitrovica too; however, the incoming chief was somewhere in the field, and the staff hadn't delivered the decision to him as yet. So there was no point of me going there. So I decided that after visiting these two secretariats and spending some time in the staff, to go back to Belgrade because there were no tasks for me to perform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Before you returned to Belgrade, were you involved in any activities in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I was at the staff HQ, the commander of the Pristina Corps telephoned the staff and wanted to speak to the staff commander and to arrange a meeting with him. We all went there together, that is to say Sreten Lukic, the head of the staff; Obrad Stevanovic; and I went to the location where the Pristina Corps staff was evacuated. General Pavkovic and General Lazarevic and Colonel Djakovic were there at the time. On the premises of the Pristina Corps, there was General Pavkovic, who, at the time, was the commander of the 1st [as interpreted] Army District; the commander of the Pristina Corps, General Lazarevic; and Colonel Djakovic, who, I think, was carrying out a different duty as opposed to the one that he did when I knew him before. That happened when he was transferred to the command. We greeted each other, after which General Pavkovic showed us a dispatch that he had received from the Chief of Staff, Ojdanic -- Chief of General Staff, Ojdanic, which envisaged resubordination of police units and organs of the interior under the Law on Defence, if I'm correct. This document virtually contained one sentence only. I read it because I was sitting next to General Pavkovic, but we were rather surprised by the content of this dispatch, especially we from the police. I told Pavkovic that it was only this morning that I had come from the ministry; we hadn't received any dispatch to this effect; and it was totally unclear to me how the Chief of General Staff was going to resubordinate organs of the interior without the knowledge of the minister of the interior. That was my objection. And I expressed my opinion that this was not how things should be done because, in any case, the minister of the interior should and must have -- should have been informed about such a decision. My objection was particularly aimed at the resubordination of the organs of the interior, as it was stated in the dispatch. I said that I was going to inform the minister about all of this because I was going back to Belgrade and that the final decision on this issue would be the minister's. I also suggested to General Pavkovic that he, on his part, also seek some additional information or instruction from the Chief of General Staff in order to clarify this sentence that was somewhat problematic with a view to the entire situation. So that was the conversation we had. We finished with this issue. And after that, I returned to Belgrade. I informed the minister about the main tasks that he sent me to Kosovo to perform and also about what I had seen in the office of the 3rd Army commander. He told me that he knew nothing of it. But having received this information from me and having been warned about some possible problems, he told me that he was going to clarify this issue. Therefore, as far as that was concerned, I thought that my role was over because he said what he said. A few days later, he informed me that the whole issue regarding resubordination and the dispatch in -- dispatching question had been settled and resolved. As far as I know, after that, MUP never received any written order or any letter from the Chief of General Staff to the effect of resubordinating units and organs of the Interior. Therefore, I believed that they resolved this issue between them, this issue of resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After this, after the 18th of April, did you ever hear about any problems relating to resubordination of police to the army?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of no instance in which any unit refused to carry out any assignment that had been incorporated and planned by the Pristina Corps and which envisaged the engagement of police, that is to say to carry out an anti-terrorist or any other operation. I know of any such incident in which orders were disobeyed [as interpreted]. There may have been some minor delays and things like that, which is normal in situations like this, but I don't know of any incident in which any of the unit failed to carry out the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, my question was: After the 18th of April until the end of the war, did you hear of anyone raising the issue of the problem of resubordination of MUP? Did you or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything about it. This question was never raised until the end of the war. The police kept doing their job in concert with the Yugoslav Army according to the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After the war, did you every hear any mention of the problem of resubordination?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear it after the war, but after the war is a different period; that was after the war. There were some stories about failure by units to resubordinate, but that primarily came from members of the Yugoslav Army. I myself didn't have any direct knowledge except of hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How did you hear about this after the war, that is to say that MUP failed to resubordinate?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the statements of General Pavkovic that the police was not resubordinated to the army. But apart from that, I have no further information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, we heard from General Vasiljevic that on the 1st of June, 1999, you were in Pristina. Were you there on that date? And tell us what you know about that in general.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that from him too. On the 1st of June, I was not in Pristina, and I did not attend any meetings where Aleksandar Vasiljevic was in attendance. I would definitely remember that. I'm certain that I did not attend the meeting he referred to, either here or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me when did you meet General Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him during a joint meeting with the Chief of the General Staff, Mr. Ojdanic. There was a MUP delegation headed by the minister. We discussed certain issues there, and it is there that I saw Aleksandar Vasiljevic for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did that meeting take place, when you met him?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first ten days of June, I think, more or less. All I can add is: Out of all those present there, I never attended a single meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Go on and perhaps then my colleague can intervene.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999, I never attended a single meeting where Momo Stojanovic was also in attendance. He was the chief of security of the Pristina Corps in 1999, although I'm not quite certain of that. In any case, we never attended the same meeting together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, Mr. Djordjevic, when did you meet General Vasiljevic in person, what month of 1999 was it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the 10th of July, 1999, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more thing, Mr. Djordjevic, General Pavkovic commanded which army?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He commanded the 3rd Army, including the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems to me that you referred to it by mistake as the 1st Army, and therefore I'm glad to have corrected that. Mr. Djordjevic, during 1999, that is to say from the beginning of 1999 until the end of the war, did you attend any meetings with the Yugoslav President, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I attended a meeting of the 4th of May, 1999, attended by the participants of some of the previous meetings I had taken place in. The Serbian president was there, the ministers of the interior, the chiefs of the General Staffs, et cetera, including the most senior officers of both the army and the police, as well as some politicians, although I don't remember which ones exactly. I attended that meeting as well on the 4th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What took place during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosovo was on the agenda as well as the rest of Serbia. The point of the meeting was to have the commander of the 3rd Army, General Pavkovic, brief the others as well as Mr. Sreten Lukic who was in charge of the MUP staff in Kosovo. Their briefings had to do about -- with the situation and other security elements in Kosovo and Metohija up to that time in wartime conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D008-4068.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 153, Mr. Djordjevic. It is 65 ter 877.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The number in line 19 may be D008-4048 instead of 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we have here the paper "Politika" of the 5th of May, 1999, containing an article about the meeting you just referred to. Does this reporting accurately reflect what took place in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The title itself says: "Tasks for the defence of the country, singling out the fight against terrorism, and general security in Kosovo and Metohija." So what was discussed were general countries [as interpreted] and the defence of the country as well as this general security situation in Kosovo. This article pretty much accurately reflects what took place in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have this document as a separate document. I think there is link to another document. I think it is a letter to the staff of the 5th or 6th of May containing a similar attachment, showing the cover page of "Politika," although I think that copy is illegible. That is why we provided this copy as well as its translation. Perhaps it might be better to introduce this document into evidence, given the fact that we have its translation and that we can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, do you know the exhibit number of the other copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately not off the cuff. It is a P number I believe. I can -- I would be able to tell you that tomorrow but not right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received, and we'd be grateful if you could let me know that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D443.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will check and advise you accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, could we have P764.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this is the minutes of the staff of the 4th of April, 1999. When did you see this document for the first time?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became familiar with all the minutes of staff sessions as I was preparing for these proceedings. That includes this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the minutes of the 4th of April, we see that all PJP detachment commanders are present, as well as those from the SAJ, JSO, as well as Mr. Stevanovic and Mr. Lukic. We can also see the agenda. I'm particularly interested in page 4 in the B/C/S, but, first of all, page 3. In the English also page 3.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is my tab number?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 3 of this document, we see forthcoming tasks issued by the head of the staff of the ministry to all those in attendance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the next page, please, in both versions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obrad Stevanovic addresses a number of issues here. He was an assistant to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is two minutes to 4.00. Can I carry on or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, let's look at D257 next. It is tab 140. Please provide us with concise answers.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of the crime police administration chief, General Ilic. He informs the SUPs and the staff that there was a change because a decree law was put into force pertaining to wartime conditions. He states that there were changes to certain rights and duties of official -- police officials when establishing criminal liability. It involved certain aspects of authority as envisaged by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, during the war, did you ever go to Kosovo and Metohija with General Ilic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999, during the war, I was never in Kosovo with Dragan Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether Dragan Ilic, during the war, visited Kosovo and Metohija; and if so, when and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was there twice, I believe. The travel orders for all chiefs of administrations in the seat of the ministry have to be signed by myself as their immediate superior; without those, they wouldn't be issued with any per diems. That is when I had occasion to see that he indeed travelled. I also know that he went there on minister's orders, that is to say the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what his tasks were when he was in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he went for the second time and returned on the 2nd of June, he came to me with a travel order, wishing to resolve the issue of per diems. He told me he had been there and that he was there to mainly instruct the chiefs of SUPs as well as to the chiefs of crime police departments in those SUPs concerning the improvement of work in on-site investigations under wartime conditions and how to provide a quality work, secure evidence, and so on and so forth. What he told me after his return was that he followed some instructions and orders that he had to convey to his chiefs in that part of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see P1050, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, now we shall see a letter of the 6th of April, 1999, with your signature. Would you please tell us briefly the subject matter and the purpose of this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By way of this dispatch, all the organisational units as well as various other entities within the SUP are informed by me about the changes concerning the disciplinary responsibility. And I highlight basic regulations and provisions of that decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see D259.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- which is tab 142 with you, Mr. Djordjevic. We will see a letter dated 9th of April on the screens, 9th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is signed by Stojan Misic, assistant minister. Please tell us what is the subject matter of this dispatch and who it was sent to?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that he was responsible for this line of work within the ministry, the line of work concerning travel and also implementation of the law on hazardous substances and their transportation, and also some decisions about domicile, residence, of citizens and identification cards, since he was in charge of all that, he sent a letter to all SUPs, all border crossing stations, as well as the staff in Pristina, informing them of these regulations and instructing them to inform all of the staff members of the changes in the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 65 ter document 5230 of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we will now see a dispatch showing that you signed it. It's dated the 11th of April, 1999. So could you, as briefly as possible, tell us what the purpose of this dispatch was and to whom it was sent.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispatch was sent on the 11th of April to all chiefs of SUPs, to commanders of all border police stations, and to the MUP staff in Pristina; and this dispatch conveys the order of the Supreme Command staff concerning the taking-in of volunteers who were foreign nationals into the units of the Yugoslav Army and what needed to be done in order for this to be implemented. So from the moment such volunteers appeared at the border crossing until they were sent to a unit, all of those steps are regulated in relation to what the staff of the MUP needed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 9260, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: D260, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering the last document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D444.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So we have 260.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this dispatch is dated 11th of April, 1999, so could you please tell us something about it.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch dated 11th of April. It says: "MUP of the Republic of Serbia UPP," which is border police administration. So this administration is sending to all SUPs and to their border police stations as well as to the MUP staff in Pristina this information concerning some obligations that federal customs administration has under a decision of the federal government and also the obligations which should be those of the border police and how they need to help the federal customs administration. So this is a dispatch containing instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see now D008-0524.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this is your tab 146.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the second page. This is a dispatch dated 18th of April, 1999. And for the Prosecution, this is 912 on the 65 ter Defence list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, briefly, what this letter is about? It was signed by you.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This letter conveys the order of the federal defence minister concerning the obligations of the army, Ministry of the Interior, and some other institutions relating to the destruction of unexploded ordnance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D445.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see D261 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- which is tab 147 in your binder, Mr. Djordjevic. And we will see that it's a dispatch dated the 19th of April, 1999, signed by Assistant Minister, General Stojan Misic. Very briefly, to whom it was sent and what is its subject matter?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch of the 19th of April was sent to all SUPs, informing them of certain obligations of the service recording the domicile and residence of citizens, plus some provisions concerning identification cards. So how to resolve certain practical issues in that domain. It was signed by assistant minister in charge of these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P1280 -- 1208.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, this is a dispatch containing instructions from the Assistant Minister, General Zekovic, who was in charge for general and joint matters. And here it deals with issues covered by the disciplinary court and higher disciplinary court. This gives further explanation to a dispatch that I sent about the newly emerged factors during the wartime situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What tab did you look at now?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I looked at 148, yes, yes. I'm looking at 148.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have something before you?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. This is a dispatch which was sent to all organisational units within the department and also outside of the department. It was sent by me on the 29th of April, and it pertains to customary procedures on promotions awarded to staff members on the occasion of the holiday of the Ministry of the Interior or it was called the security -- security forces day, the 13th of May. Certain people were given awards on that day. And this document contains proposals for who should be given such an award.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could we have D262 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- which is your tab 148.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tendering that last one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have it already -- it's already in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, here, are some additional pieces of information by General Zekovic. They were sent to the organisational units of the department. Since he was in charge of everything relating to the disciplinary court and higher disciplinary court, this is just a further explanation of my previous dispatch concerning disciplinary proceedings in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D008-0637, 65 ter 928.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 150, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a letter in which on the 29th of April, 1999, Minister Stojiljkovic informs the President of Serbia, Milan Milutinovic, on damage to road bridges, railway bridges, main roads, and all those locations where this infrastructure was damaged and what reparations were made and how the traffic was redirected and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D446.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, we're right on the crunch point of time with the tape. Where are you situated?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm at the very end, Your Honours. I think that I won't need more than half an hour and maybe quite a bit less than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll look forward then to hearing you tomorrow at 2.15 for quarter of an hour, Mr. Djurdjic. But I think we have covered a lot of ground today. I thank you for that. But we will need to be watching time closely. We adjourn now until 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of December, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.20 p.m.,
